title: U.S. House · Oklahoma's 4th District
area: South-central Oklahoma, including Norman, Lawton and Ada

candidates.name: Tom Cole

summary.text: Tom Cole is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 4th District, seeking re-election.

positions.summary: His official site says overly broad executive orders and legislative proposals that limit the rights of law-abiding gun owners are not the answer to gun violence.
positions.quote: overly broad executive orders and legislative proposals that limit the rights of law-abiding gun owners are not the answer to gun violence.

positions.summary: In a June 2026 statement he said he supported the Secure America Act, which funds ICE and Border Patrol personnel and immigration enforcement operations, and has consistently voted to resource them.
positions.quote: It’s exactly why I have consistently voted to comprehensively resource these law enforcement professionals as they carry out their security missions.

record.text: Voted in favor of the Water Resources Development Act of 2026.
Introduced companion legislation supporting the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma, which passed the U.S. House and was sent to the White House.
Introduced a resolution congratulating the University of Oklahoma baseball team for winning the 2026 Men's College World Series.

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately. Ballotpedia's biography page for Cole returned no usable content at the time of research; record items are drawn instead from his official House press releases.

candidates.name: Mitchell Jacob

summary.text: Mitchell Jacob is an Army veteran, public defender and OU Law graduate running as the Democratic candidate on fiscal responsibility, public education and criminal justice reform.

background.text: Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma; served in the U.S. Army from 2017 to 2022 as a Sergeant and Cryptologic Linguist, deploying to southern Syria in support of Operation Inherent Resolve.

Earned a high school diploma from Boulder Creek High School, an associate degree from Rio Salado College (2016), a bachelor's degree from Grand Canyon University (2019), and a law degree from the University of Oklahoma College of Law (2025).
Career experience includes working as a stockbroker, banker, mortgage loan originator, and public defender.

priorities.text: Says the rapidly growing federal deficit and national debt is the biggest threat facing the country, and calls for spending cuts and reduced tax expenditures.
priorities.quote: The biggest threat to our democracy is our skyrocketing national debt. … We need to stop raising the debt limit, cut spending, greatly reduce our tax expenditures, and eliminate the federal debt.

priorities.text: Advocates for quality public education, small businesses, job creation, livable wages and human rights.
As a public defender, prioritizes criminal justice reform centered on rehabilitation over punishment.
priorities.quote: I believe that the first pillar of criminal justice is rehabilitation, and then it is punishment.

positions.summary: His campaign site says to abolish ICE and require body cameras and transparency, and says the immigration system needs capacity rather than more law enforcement.
His campaign site describes him as pro-choice and says a woman's rights should remain consistent regardless of state lines.
positions.quote: A woman's rights should remain consistent regardless of state lines.

positions.summary: His campaign site says the U.S. must cease all economic, political and military support for Israel until it ends its campaign of violence.
positions.quote: I believe the United States must cease all economic, political, and military support for Israel until they cease their campaign of violence and aggression.

positions.summary: In a campaign blog post he criticized the administration's tariffs, including those on Canada, and said Congress must reassert its constitutional role over tariffs.
positions.quote: Congress must reassert its constitutional role to prevent unilateral tariff shifts and prevent instability.

positions.summary: In a September 2026 campaign blog post on the Iran war, he said the House and Senate must pass a War Powers Resolution and that no congressional authorization preceded the war.
positions.quote: The House must pass another War Powers Resolution, and the Senate must pass it as well.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located; positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
